title: The Staircase of Ethics: Probing LLM Value Priorities through Multi-Step Induction to Complex Moral Dilemmas
findings: Models generally ranked 'sanctity' lower than 'care' and 'fairness', but its preference was highly volatile across dilemma stages and varied between models. The 'sanctity' dimension was also involved in non-transitive reasoning cycles (e.g., care > sanctity, sanctity > fairness, but care ≈ fairness), suggesting context-driven imitation rather than stable principles. Preference for 'tradition' also varied significantly, with some models showing strong support (GLM-4-Plus) and others showing dramatic fluctuations (Llama).
references: Marwa Abdulhai, Gregory Serapio-Garcia, Clément Crepy, Daria Valter, John Canny, and Natasha Jaques. 2023. Moral foundations of large language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.15337.

measurement_description: Measurement of LLMs' value preferences for 'sanctity' (upholding purity, sacredness) and 'tradition' (respect for cultural or religious customs) when placed in conflict with other moral values (e.g., care, fairness, liberty) across a series of escalating moral dilemmas.
